title: Getting Started with maxentcpp
text: maxentcpp ships cropped bioclimatic raster stack (bio1: Annual Mean Temperature, bio12: Annual Precipitation) 73 GBIF occurrence records Abeillia abeillei.
code: library(maxentcpp) library(terra) #> terra 1.9.34  # Load environmental layers stack_path      <- system.file("extdata", "stack_1_12_crop.rds",                                package = "maxentcpp") example_rasters <- terra::unwrap(readRDS(stack_path)) bio1  <- example_rasters[[1]] bio12 <- example_rasters[[2]]  # Convert to maxentcpp grid objects g_bio1  <- maxent_grid_from_terra(bio1) g_bio12 <- maxent_grid_from_terra(bio12)  # Load occurrence records data(example_occ_df) head(example_occ_df) #>             species    long    lat #> 1 Abeillia abeillei -92.933 15.733 #> 2 Abeillia abeillei -93.192 15.880 #> 3 Abeillia abeillei -92.632 15.420 #> 4 Abeillia abeillei -92.741 15.644 #> 5 Abeillia abeillei -92.229 15.158 #> 6 Abeillia abeillei -93.093 15.823

title: Getting Started with maxentcpp
text: Create grid dimension object matches environmental layers, convert occurrence lon/lat coordinates grid row/column indices:
code: info <- maxent_grid_info(g_bio1) dim  <- maxent_dimension(nrows    = info$nrows,                          ncols    = info$ncols,                          xll      = info$xll,                          yll      = info$yll,                          cellsize = info$cellsize)  occ <- maxent_read_occurrences(example_occ_df, dim,                                lon_col = "long",                                lat_col = "lat")  cat("Presence points:", length(occ$indices), "\n") #> Presence points: 73

title: Getting Started with maxentcpp
text: Maxent contrasts presence locations random sample background points. default 10 000 background points standard practice:
code: bg <- maxent_background_indices(g_bio1, n = 10000, seed = 42) cat("Background points:", length(bg$indices), "\n") #> Background points: 2371

what: Extract Environmental Values and Generate Features
title: Getting Started with maxentcpp
text: Extract environmental variable values point locations (background + presence) generate feature transformations (linear, quadratic, hinge):
code: all_rows <- c(bg$rows, occ$rows) all_cols <- c(bg$cols, occ$cols) n_total  <- length(all_rows)  # 0-based indices of the presence samples within the combined vector sample_indices <- seq(length(bg$rows), n_total - 1L)  # Extract environmental values at all locations bio1_vals  <- sapply(seq_along(all_rows), function(i)     grid_get_value(g_bio1,  all_rows[i], all_cols[i])) bio12_vals <- sapply(seq_along(all_rows), function(i)     grid_get_value(g_bio12, all_rows[i], all_cols[i]))  env_data <- list(bio1 = bio1_vals, bio12 = bio12_vals)  features <- maxent_generate_features(env_data,                                      types    = c("linear", "quadratic", "hinge"),                                      n_hinges = 15) cat("Generated", length(features), "features\n") #> Generated 64 features

title: Getting Started with maxentcpp
text: Compute Area ROC Curve (AUC) metrics comparing predictions presence sites versus background sites:
code: pres_preds <- maxent_extract_predictions_raw(     fs, list(g_bio1, g_bio12), c("bio1", "bio12"),     occ$rows, occ$cols)  bg_preds <- maxent_extract_predictions_raw(     fs, list(g_bio1, g_bio12), c("bio1", "bio12"),     bg$rows, bg$cols)  eval_result <- maxent_evaluate(pres_preds, bg_preds) cat("AUC:", round(eval_result$auc, 4), "\n") #> AUC: 0.8033 cat("Max Kappa:", round(eval_result$max_kappa, 4), "\n") #> Max Kappa: 0.1834

title: MaxEnt Features and Outputs
text: Maxent fits probability distribution geographic space maximizing entropy subject constraints derived training data. Given set environmental variables measured presence locations, algorithm finds distribution : Agrees observed data (sample expectations match model expectations feature). spread (high entropy) possible, avoiding unwarranted assumptions. result Gibbs distribution: P(x)=1Zexp⁡(∑jλjfj(x)) P(x) = \frac{1}{Z} \exp\left(\sum_j \lambda_j f_j(x)\right) fjf_j features (transformations environmental variables), λj\lambda_j learned weights, ZZ normalizing constant (partition function).

title: MaxEnt Features and Outputs
text: Features transformations raw environmental variables. feature type captures different aspect species–environment relationship. maxentcpp implements five feature types Java Maxent 3.4.4:

title: MaxEnt Features and Outputs
text: simplest transformation: linear rescaling [0, 1]. flinear(v)=v−vminvmax−vmin f_{\text{linear}}(v) = \frac{v - v_{\min}}{v_{\max} - v_{\min}} Linear features capture monotonic (directional) responses. example, species prefers warmer temperatures positive λ\lambda linear feature mean annual temperature.

title: MaxEnt Features and Outputs
text: square linear feature: fquadratic(v)=flinear(v)2 f_{\text{quadratic}}(v) = f_{\text{linear}}(v)^2 Quadratic features allow model capture unimodal (hump-shaped) responses — species may prefer intermediate values variable, declining extremes.

title: MaxEnt Features and Outputs
text: product two linear features different variables: fproduct(v1,v2)=flinear(v1)×flinear(v2) f_{\text{product}}(v_1, v_2) = f_{\text{linear}}(v_1) \times f_{\text{linear}}(v_2) Product features model interactions environmental variables. example, species might tolerate low precipitation temperatures also low.
code: maxent_product_feature(env_values_1, env_values_2,                        min1, max1, min2, max2)

title: MaxEnt Features and Outputs
text: binary step function: fthreshold(v)={1if v≥t0otherwise f_{\text{threshold}}(v) = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{} v \geq t \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} Threshold features capture hard limits — example, species survive critical temperature.

title: MaxEnt Features and Outputs
text: piecewise linear function zero one side linear : fhinge(v)={0if v≤knotv−knotvmax−knotif v>knot f_{\text{hinge}}(v) = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{} v \leq \text{knot} \\ \frac{v - \text{knot}}{v_{\max} - \text{knot}} & \text{} v > \text{knot} \end{cases} (Reverse hinges ramp instead .) Hinge features expressive feature type Maxent. set evenly-spaced hinges can approximate smooth response curve, similar basis spline. default feature type datasets ≥15\geq 15 presence records.

title: MaxEnt Features and Outputs
text: Maxent uses sequential coordinate ascent (also called sequential updating) maximize penalized log-likelihood. iteration, algorithm: Selects one feature fjf_j. Finds optimal step size α\alpha maximizes gain (regularized log-likelihood improvement) feature. Updates λj←λj+α\lambda_j \leftarrow \lambda_j + \alpha. Recalculates model distribution. process repeats, cycling features, convergence (gain per iteration falls threshold, typically 10−510^{-5}).

title: MaxEnt Features and Outputs
text: Without regularization, Maxent can overfit noise training data. algorithm applies L1 regularization (lasso penalty) controlled beta_multiplier parameter: beta_multiplier = 1.0 (default): standard regularization Java Maxent. beta_multiplier > 1.0: stronger regularization, simpler models. beta_multiplier < 1.0: weaker regularization, complex models. regularization parameter feature depends type. Hinge threshold features receive higher penalties linear features, reflecting greater risk overfitting flexible feature types.

title: MaxEnt Features and Outputs
text: trained model produces raw output values (unnormalized Gibbs scores). transformed ecologically interpretable quantities using one three transformations:

title: MaxEnt Features and Outputs
text: raw(x)=exp⁡(∑jλjfj(x))Z \text{raw}(x) = \frac{\exp\left(\sum_j \lambda_j f_j(x)\right)}{Z} Z=∑xexp⁡(∑jλjfj(x))Z = \sum_x \exp\left(\sum_j \lambda_j f_j(x)\right) density normalizer (sum background cells). Raw output represents relative occurrence rate (ROR). cell raw value 2.0 twice expected occurrence rate cell value 1.0.

title: MaxEnt Features and Outputs
text: cloglog(x)=1−exp⁡(−eH⋅raw(x)) \text{cloglog}(x) = 1 - \exp\left(-e^H \cdot \text{raw}(x)\right) HH model entropy. Cloglog output recommended default since Maxent 3.4.0. certain assumptions sampling process, cloglog values can interpreted probability species present grid cell, conditional environment. Values [0, 1].

title: MaxEnt Features and Outputs
text: logistic(x)=eH⋅raw(x)1+eH⋅raw(x) \text{logistic}(x) = \frac{e^H \cdot \text{raw}(x)}{1 + e^H \cdot \text{raw}(x)} Logistic output default Maxent 3.4.0. Like cloglog, values [0, 1], probabilistic interpretation requires stronger assumption (species prevalence = 0.5). cloglog transform now preferred applications.

text: See inst/examples/quickstart.R complete workflow including variable importance, response curves, MESS analysis, clamping.
code: library(maxentcpp) library(terra)  # --- 1. Load raster data from the package ----------------------------------- stack_path      <- system.file("extdata", "stack_1_12_crop.rds",                                package = "maxentcpp") example_rasters <- terra::unwrap(readRDS(stack_path)) g_bio1  <- maxent_grid_from_terra(example_rasters[[1]]) g_bio12 <- maxent_grid_from_terra(example_rasters[[2]])  # --- 2. Occurrence records --------------------------------------------------- data(example_occ_df)   # columns: species, long, lat info <- maxent_grid_info(g_bio1) dim  <- maxent_dimension(info$nrows, info$ncols,                          info$xll, info$yll, info$cellsize) occ  <- maxent_read_occurrences(example_occ_df, dim,                                 lon_col = "long", lat_col = "lat")  # --- 3. Background points ---------------------------------------------------- bg <- maxent_background_indices(g_bio1, n = 10000, seed = 42)  # --- 4. Features ------------------------------------------------------------- all_rows <- c(bg$rows, occ$rows) all_cols <- c(bg$cols, occ$cols) n_total  <- length(all_rows) sample_indices <- seq(length(bg$rows), n_total - 1L)  bio1_vals  <- sapply(seq_along(all_rows), function(i)     grid_get_value(g_bio1,  all_rows[i], all_cols[i])) bio12_vals <- sapply(seq_along(all_rows), function(i)     grid_get_value(g_bio12, all_rows[i], all_cols[i]))  features <- maxent_generate_features(     list(bio1 = bio1_vals, bio12 = bio12_vals),     types = c("linear", "quadratic", "hinge"), n_hinges = 15)  # --- 5. Train ---------------------------------------------------------------- fs     <- maxent_featured_space(n_total, as.integer(sample_indices), features) result <- maxent_fit(fs, max_iter = 500, convergence = 1e-5) cat("AUC:", maxent_evaluate(     maxent_extract_predictions(fs, list(g_bio1, g_bio12),                                c("bio1", "bio12"), occ$rows, occ$cols),     maxent_extract_predictions(fs, list(g_bio1, g_bio12),                                c("bio1", "bio12"), bg$rows,  bg$cols))$auc, "\n")  # --- 6. Project and visualise ------------------------------------------------ pred_raster <- maxent_grid_to_terra(     maxent_project_cloglog(fs, list(g_bio1, g_bio12), c("bio1", "bio12"))) terra::plot(pred_raster,             main = "Predicted Habitat Suitability (cloglog)",             col  = hcl.colors(50, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE))

title: maxentcpp 1.0.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-05-18 Initial CRAN release. C++17 implementation Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) species distribution modeling algorithm R bindings via Rcpp. Core features: linear, quadratic, product, hinge, threshold feature transformations. Categorical variable support via BinaryFeature class — one binary indicator per distinct level, matching Java Maxent’s BinaryFeature.java. Use categorical parameter maxent_generate_features() maxent_run(). Missing data handling: maxent_complete_cases() filters samples NA, NaN, NODATA sentinel values (-9999); maxent_impute_means() provides mean-substitution. maxent_run() now automatically removes NODATA samples. Cross-validation via maxent_cross_validate() — stratified k-fold partitioning matching Java Maxent’s SampleSet.splitForCV(). Replicate runs via maxent_replicate() — bootstrap subsample resampling matching Java Maxent’s SampleSet.replicate(). Jackknife variable importance via maxent_jackknife() — leave-one--one variable importance analysis matching Java Maxent’s Runner.jackknifeGain(). Spatial projection raw, logistic, complementary log-log (cloglog) scales. Terra-native raster /O streaming evaluation low memory usage. Model diagnostics: AUC, variable importance (percent contribution permutation importance), response curves, MESS maps. Lambda file /O compatible original Java MaxEnt software. Fixed duplicate C++ R function definitions caused compilation errors certain build configurations.
